questions.question: For each pathogen, what is the animal reservoir?
questions.question_raw: For each virus, what is the animal reservoir?
questions.model_answer: a) Herpes B (Macacine herpesvirus 1): macaque monkeys (Old World macaques, e.g. rhesus and cynomolgus). b) Sin Nombre virus: the deer mouse, Peromyscus maniculatus. c) Rabies: mammalian reservoirs vary by region—in North America, bats plus terrestrial carnivores (raccoons, skunks, foxes); worldwide the dog is the dominant reservoir. d) Chlamydia psittaci: psittacine birds (parrots, parakeets, cockatiels) and other birds.

cohort_answer.text: Herpes B: Macaque monkey. Sin Nombre virus: Deer mouse/rat. Rabies: Bats and raccoons. Chlamydia psittaci: Parrots.

questions.question: A 30-year-old man from Ukraine lives in Ottawa. He sometimes goes camping in the Ottawa river valley and sometimes to northwestern Ontario. He recently went on a business trip to Arizona. He also owns two parrots. He presents with a non-resolving pneumonia; chest CT shows left upper lobe consolidation. He was treated with cefuroxime and did not improve. In the table, fill out the possible etiologies of the pneumonia (genus and species) and their associated epidemiological risk factor.
questions.question_raw: Q21 (2018). 30 yo man from Ukraine lives in Ottawa. He sometimes goes camping in the Ottawa river valley and sometimes goes to northwestern Ontario. He recently went on a business trip to Arizona. He also owns two parrots. He now presents with a non-resolving pneumonia. Chest CT shows left upper lobe consolidation. He was treated with cefuroxime and did not get better.

parts.text: Fill out the possible etiologies of the pneumonia (genus and species) and the associated epidemiological risk factor for: Mycobacterium tuberculosis; Blastomyces dermatitidis; Chlamydia psittaci; Coccidioides immitis/posadasii; Histoplasma capsulatum.

parts_raw.text: In the table, fill out the possible etiologies of the pneumonia (genus and species) and its associated epidemiological risk factor. Organism | Epidemiological Risk Factor: Mycobacterium tuberculosis; Blastomyces dermatitidis; Chlamydia psittaci; Coccidioides immitis/posadasii; Histoplasma capsulatum

questions.model_answer: Mycobacterium tuberculosis — emigrant from Ukraine (high-incidence country). Blastomyces dermatitidis — camping in northwestern Ontario (Great Lakes/soil exposure). Histoplasma capsulatum — Ottawa river valley (river-valley soil, bird/bat droppings). Coccidioides immitis/posadasii — travel to Arizona (desert southwest). Chlamydia psittaci — parrot ownership (psittacine bird exposure).
questions.beyond_mandell: Epidemiologic associations for the endemic fungi and C. psittaci are from established knowledge/other Mandell chapters; not in this TB chapter.

cohort_answer.text: Blastomyces dermatitidis - Northwestern Ontario; Histoplasma capsulatum - Ottawa river valley; Chlamydia psittaci - Parrot owner; Coccidioides immitis - Arizona; Mycobacterium tuberculosis - Ukraine
